Indian stock market benchmarks ended sharply higher on Friday, with the Sensex jumping 879 points, or 1.23 percent, to 72,472 and the Nifty gaining 289 points, or 1.30 percent, to close at 22,520.
IT led sectoral gains with a 3.02 percent surge, while FMCG rose 2.2 percent and PSU banks gained 1.63 percent. Midcaps advanced 1.56 percent and smallcaps rose 0.54 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading with a gains of 44.5 points at around 22,645 in early trade, indicating positive opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Down)

Asian share markets got off to a cautious start on Monday as earnings season loomed as a challenge to sky-high tech valuations, while oil was choppy after strikes on shipping and airports in the Gulf.
US Equities (Up)

Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to ​next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's ‌next policy decision.

The Dow Jones ​Industrial Average rose 423.31 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, the S&P 500 gained 46.15 points, or 0.59%, to 7,811.51 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 172.83 points, or 0.64%, ‌to 27,366.17.
Dollar Index (Down)
The dollar index held near 17-month highs at 102, but has stalled on the yen at 158.15 as the threat of Japanese intervention deters speculators for now.
US Bond Yield (Flat)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasuries remained unchanged at 5.23% and 4.78%, respectively, in the early trade on Monday.
Asian Currencies (Gain)

Asian currencies traded higher against the US dollar, with the South Korean Won leading the gains, rising 0.355% from its previous close. The Philippine Peso advanced 0.204%, followed by the Chinese Renminbi, which gained 0.158%, while the Japanese Yen strengthened 0.12%. The Indonesian Rupiah and Thai baht edged up 0.089% and 0.087%, respectively. The Singapore Dollar rose 0.078%, while the Malaysian Ringgit and Taiwan Dollar posted modest gains of 0.059% and 0.041%, respectively.
Crude (Slips)

Oil prices slipped on Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow.
Brent crude futures fell $1.57, to $102.58 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $89.96 a barrel, down $1.85, or 2.01%.
Gold (Up)

Gold edged higher as traders assessed US President Donald Trump’s claim of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, even as risks of a widening conflict in the Middle East raised inflation concerns. Bullion traded near $4,200 an ounce, after rising 1.3% last week.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their selling streak for the 11th consecutive session on October 9, offloading equities worth Rs 3568 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued their buying support, purchasing equities worth around Rs 4743 crore during the session.
